lines.text: Why do highways have those textured grooves cut into the shoulder that make a loud buzzing vibration?
Those grooves are called rumble strips, and they are one of the most effective safety inventions on Earth.
Fatigue and distraction cause thousands of drivers to unintentionally drift off the roadway.
When vehicle tires roll over the milled asphalt grooves, it creates intense tactile vibrations and a loud drone.
This physical jolt instantly shocks drowsy or inattentive drivers awake before they crash into trees.
Federal studies show rumble strips reduce fatal run-off-the-road crashes by over thirty-five percent.
Those humble grooves in the pavement silently save thousands of lives every single year.
